question: The sandwich is divided along its diagonal. What fraction is the coloured piece?
options: A. One quarter | B. One half | C. One eighth
explanation: The diagonal divides the square sandwich into 2 equal-sized pieces. One piece is one half. Hint: Look at the number of equal parts in the whole.

question: The square tile has 4 equal sections. What fraction of the tile is coloured?
options: A. One quarter | B. One half | C. One eighth
explanation: One of the 4 equal sections is coloured, so it is one quarter. Hint: Count the equal sections, including the uncoloured ones.
visual_description: A square has four equal square sections, one coloured.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A cake is cut into the 4 pieces shown. Are all the pieces quarters?
options: A. Yes; any 4 pieces are quarters | B. No; quarters need 8 pieces | C. No; the pieces are not equal in size
correct_answer: No; the pieces are not equal in size
explanation: Four pieces are quarters only when they are equal-sized parts of the same whole. Hint: Compare the widths of these pieces.
visual_description: A rectangular cake has four strips with widths in the ratio 1, 1, 2 and 4.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: You fold a rectangular card to make 2 equal parts. Where should the fold go?
options: A. Very close to one edge | B. Through the middle, with opposite edges meeting | C. Anywhere, as long as there is one fold
correct_answer: Through the middle, with opposite edges meeting
explanation: Bringing opposite edges together makes a fold through the middle and two matching halves. Hint: Both parts must cover the same amount of card.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: Four people share one flatbread equally, with none left over. What fraction of the flatbread does each receive?
options: A. One quarter | B. One half | C. One eighth
explanation: Each person receives one of 4 equal shares of the whole flatbread. Hint: The whole is one flatbread.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: One tray of slice is cut into 8 equal portions for 8 people. What does “one eighth” mean here?
options: A. All 8 portions together | B. One person’s portion | C. Any 2 portions together
explanation: One eighth is one of the tray’s 8 equal portions. All 8 portions make the whole tray. Hint: Identify the whole before naming a part.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A music session lasts one hour. A break begins halfway through. What fraction of the hour has passed?
options: A. One quarter | B. One eighth | C. One half
explanation: Halfway divides the hour into 2 equal durations. One has passed and one remains. Hint: Think of two equal parts of the session.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A game has 4 periods of equal length. What fraction of the playing time is one period?
options: A. One quarter | B. One half | C. One eighth
explanation: One period is one of 4 equal parts of the total playing time. Hint: The periods must last equally long.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A dance routine has 8 sections that take equal time. One section is finished. What fraction of the routine’s time is finished?
options: A. One eighth | B. One quarter | C. One half
explanation: One completed section out of 8 equal-duration sections is one eighth of the total time. Hint: Count equal durations, not the number of different movements.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: One ribbon is marked into 4 equal lengths. How many of these lengths should be coloured to show half the ribbon?
options: A. 1 length | B. 4 lengths | C. 2 lengths
explanation: Two quarter-lengths cover half of the ribbon, leaving two quarter-lengths uncoloured. Hint: Make two equal groups of the four lengths.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: One chocolate bar has 8 equal squares. How many squares make one quarter of the bar?
options: A. 4 squares | B. 2 squares | C. 1 square
explanation: Divide the 8 squares into 4 equal groups. Each group has 2 squares and is one quarter. Hint: Make four equal shares of the whole bar.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A walking route is split into 8 equal lengths. How many lengths take you halfway along the route?
options: A. 2 lengths | B. 8 lengths | C. 4 lengths
explanation: Four of the 8 equal lengths make half the route. Four equal lengths remain. Hint: Halfway leaves the same distance still to walk.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A paper strip already has 4 equal sections. How can you turn it into eighths?
options: A. Divide every section into 2 equal parts | B. Divide just one section into 2 parts | C. Erase all but one dividing line
correct_answer: Divide every section into 2 equal parts
explanation: Splitting each of the 4 equal sections in half makes 8 equal parts of the original strip. Hint: Every section needs the same change.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: Each card has one coloured part. Which cards show one half coloured?
options: A. Only A | B. Both A and B | C. Only B
explanation: A is divided vertically and B diagonally. Each division makes 2 equal-area parts, with one coloured. Hint: Halves can have different shapes.
visual_description: Card A is split vertically into two equal rectangles, one coloured. Card B is split diagonally into two equal triangles, one coloured.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: Two identical mats are divided differently. A has 4 equal strips; B has 4 equal rectangles in two rows. Is one part of either mat a quarter?
options: A. Only A, because quarters must be strips | B. Yes; both mats have 4 equal-sized parts | C. Only B, because quarters must be in two rows
correct_answer: Yes; both mats have 4 equal-sized parts
explanation: Quarters describe 4 equal parts of a whole, not one particular shape of part. Hint: Check equal size and the number of parts.
visual_description: Identical rectangular mats: A has four equal vertical strips, B a two-by-two grid of equal rectangles. One part is coloured in each.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A show has 4 acts, but one act lasts much longer than the others. Is every act one quarter of the show’s time?
options: A. No; the acts do not take equal time | B. Yes; there are 4 acts | C. Yes; every act has a name
correct_answer: No; the acts do not take equal time
explanation: Four named stages are not quarters of the time unless their durations are equal. Hint: Equal fractions of time need equal durations.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A straight-sided container has the same width and depth from bottom to top. It is filled to the middle line. What fraction of its capacity is filled?
options: A. One quarter | B. One eighth | C. One half
explanation: Because the width and depth stay the same, the middle line splits the capacity into 2 equal amounts. Hint: The container has the same shape all the way up.
visual_description: A uniform straight-sided container is filled to the middle of its height.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: Which is the smaller portion of the same loaf: one quarter or one eighth?
options: A. One eighth | B. One quarter | C. They are equal
explanation: Sharing the same loaf into 8 equal portions makes smaller portions than sharing it into 4. Hint: Keep the whole loaf the same.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A half of a small cake and a half of a much larger cake are served. Must the pieces be the same size?
options: A. Yes; all halves are the same size | B. No; the whole cakes are different sizes | C. Yes; cutting always makes equal pieces across different cakes
correct_answer: No; the whole cakes are different sizes
explanation: A half depends on the size of its whole. Half of the larger cake can be larger. Hint: Ask which whole each half belongs to.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: The strip represents a game divided into 4 equal playing periods. The coloured periods are finished. What fraction of playing time is finished?
options: A. One quarter | B. One eighth | C. One half
explanation: Two of 4 equal periods are finished. Two quarters make one half. Hint: Compare the finished time with the time still to play.
visual_description: One game is represented by four equal sections; the first two are coloured.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A pizza has 8 slices, but one slice is much bigger than the others. Why can’t every slice be called one eighth?
options: A. A pizza cannot have eighths | B. Eighths must be square | C. Eighths must be equal portions of the whole pizza
correct_answer: Eighths must be equal portions of the whole pizza
explanation: Counting 8 slices is not enough: all 8 must be equal portions for each to be one eighth. Hint: Check the sizes as well as the count.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: Draw two identical rectangular flags. Divide one into halves and colour one half. Divide the other into quarters and colour one quarter.
correct_answer: Each flag represents one whole. The first has 2 equal parts with 1 coloured; the second has 4 equal parts with 1 coloured.
explanation: Each flag represents one whole. The first has 2 equal parts with 1 coloured; the second has 4 equal parts with 1 coloured. Hint: Accept different valid partitions. Require equal-area parts, exactly one part coloured in each flag and labels “half” and “quarter”.
acceptance_note: Accept different valid partitions. Require equal-area parts, exactly one part coloured in each flag and labels “half” and “quarter”.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: Draw a strip to represent a performance with 8 stages that take equal time. Mark the end of the first stage and label the time used.
correct_answer: A whole strip divided into 8 equal sections, with the first section identified as one eighth of the performance’s time.
explanation: A whole strip divided into 8 equal sections, with the first section identified as one eighth of the performance’s time. Hint: Require eight equal sections and one eighth correctly marked. Do not require minutes or fraction symbols.
acceptance_note: Require eight equal sections and one eighth correctly marked. Do not require minutes or fraction symbols.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A square napkin is divided into two equal rectangles. One rectangle is coloured. What fraction is coloured?
options: A. One quarter | B. One eighth | C. One half
explanation: One of 2 equal parts is one half of the whole napkin. Hint: Include the uncoloured part when counting the whole.
visual_description: A square napkin has two equal horizontal sections, one coloured.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: The garden plan is split into the equal sections shown. What fraction is the coloured flower bed?
options: A. One quarter | B. One eighth | C. One half
explanation: The coloured bed is one of 4 equal parts of the whole garden plan. Hint: Count all the equal sections.
visual_description: A rectangular garden plan has four equal strips, one coloured.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A rectangular snack is cut into 8 equal pieces. One piece is packed for lunch. What fraction of the whole snack is packed?
options: A. One quarter | B. One eighth | C. One half
explanation: One of 8 equal pieces is one eighth of the snack. Hint: Name one equal part of a whole divided into eight.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: Which cut gives two people half of one sandwich each?
options: A. A cut making 1 large and 1 small piece | B. A cut making 2 equal-sized pieces | C. A cut taking off one small corner
explanation: Each half must be the same-sized part of the whole sandwich. Hint: Two pieces alone do not guarantee halves.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A practice session has 4 activities that last equally long. What fraction of the total activity time is the first activity?
options: A. One half | B. One eighth | C. One quarter
explanation: The activity uses one of 4 equal durations. Hint: Use the equal time, not the activity’s name.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: Eight equally long songs make up a concert. After one song, what fraction of the singing time has passed?
options: A. One eighth | B. One quarter | C. One half
explanation: One of 8 equal song durations is one eighth of the singing time. Hint: Count equal-duration parts of the concert.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A timer divides one hour into 4 equal stretches. What is one stretch called?
options: A. A quarter of an hour | B. Half an hour | C. An eighth of an hour
explanation: A quarter of an hour is one of 4 equal durations making up the hour. Hint: The whole time is one hour.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A border has 8 equal panels. How many panels should be painted to show one quarter of the border?
options: A. 1 panel | B. 4 panels | C. 2 panels
explanation: Four equal groups of 2 panels make all 8 panels, so one group is one quarter. Hint: Share the panels into four equal groups.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A swimming practice has 8 equal lengths. After how many lengths is half the distance finished?
options: A. 2 lengths | B. 4 lengths | C. 6 lengths
explanation: Four equal lengths are half of eight; four lengths remain. Hint: Half the distance is equal to the distance left.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A square is cut diagonally into 2 matching triangles. Can one triangle represent half a square?
options: A. Yes; the triangles cover equal areas | B. No; halves must be rectangles | C. No; triangles only show quarters
correct_answer: Yes; the triangles cover equal areas
explanation: The two matching triangles together make the square, so each is one half. Hint: The shape of a part does not decide its fraction.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A trip has 8 stages with very different journey times. Is the first stage necessarily one eighth of the trip’s time?
options: A. Yes; it is one of 8 stages | B. No; the times are not equal | C. Yes; it happens first
correct_answer: No; the times are not equal
explanation: With unequal stage times, counting one stage out of eight does not tell us what fraction of the total time it takes. Hint: Check whether the measured parts are equal.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: The same sheet can be cut into equal halves or equal quarters. Which cut makes smaller pieces?
options: A. Halves | B. Both make pieces of the same size | C. Quarters
explanation: Four equal parts of the same sheet are smaller than two equal parts. Hint: The whole sheet stays the same size.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A straight-sided tank has a uniform width and depth. Its height is marked into 4 equal sections. The lowest section is full of water. What fraction of the tank’s capacity is filled?
options: A. One half | B. One eighth | C. One quarter
explanation: The 4 equal-height sections have equal capacities because the tank’s width and depth stay the same. One is filled. Hint: One of four equal amounts is filled.
visual_description: A uniform tank is marked into four equal-height sections; water fills the lowest section.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A whole bread roll is cut into 8 equal pieces. Seven pieces are on a plate. How many more eighths are needed to complete the roll?
options: A. 1 eighth | B. 2 eighths | C. 4 eighths
explanation: Eight eighths make the roll. Seven are present, so one more is needed. Hint: Count the missing equal part.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: A paper model has 4 parts. What must you check before labelling each part a quarter?
options: A. All 4 parts have different colours | B. All 4 parts cover equal amounts of the paper | C. All 4 parts have names
correct_answer: All 4 parts cover equal amounts of the paper
explanation: Each quarter must be one of 4 equal-area parts of the original paper. Hint: The number of parts is only part of the check.

skill_title: Halves, quarters and eighths in everyday contexts
question: Draw one rectangular fruit bar. Divide the whole bar into eighths and colour one portion. Label that portion.
correct_answer: One whole rectangle split into 8 equal-area parts, with exactly one part coloured and labelled “one eighth”.
explanation: One whole rectangle split into 8 equal-area parts, with exactly one part coloured and labelled “one eighth”. Hint: Accept eight equal strips, a 2-by-4 grid or another valid equal-area partition. Check that the whole bar is represented.
acceptance_note: Accept eight equal strips, a 2-by-4 grid or another valid equal-area partition. Check that the whole bar is represented.
